learningObjective: Understand how StableHLO represents dynamic shapes and identify true statements about StableHLO's design intent regarding portability and shape.
stem: Consider StableHLO as a portable, framework-independent operator set. Which of the following statements about StableHLO's design regarding shapes and portability are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: StableHLO is intended as a portable operator set that decouples ML frameworks from any single compiler backend; multiple backends (XLA, IREE, etc.) can consume the same StableHLO program.

StableHLO forbids any dynamic-shape tensor: all shapes must be statically known at graph-construction time, so any framework that emits StableHLO must specialize the graph for every observed input shape.
StableHLO supports both fully static and dynamically-shaped tensors; dynamic dims are represented with `?` on the tensor type, optionally with per-dim bounds attributes.
StableHLO includes device-placement and stream-scheduling attributes as first-class parts of every op, so it is a single-source-of-truth for runtime execution details.

explanation: StableHLO is a stability-tracked op set designed as a portable interchange format between ML frameworks and compilers (successor to HLO for that role). It supports both static and dynamic shapes, with dynamic dims written as `?` and optional bounds. It does not embed device placement or stream scheduling — those are the domain of runtimes and higher-level pipelines, not the op set itself.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: portability is StableHLO's stated design goal.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: StableHLO's shape system covers both static and dynamic dims (with bounds).
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: device placement / streams are runtime concerns; StableHLO is a math-level op set.

assumptions: Reference is to StableHLO's specification as of 2024-2026; details evolve but the design intent is stable.
nonImplications: Does not imply every StableHLO op has a specific implementation on every backend; portability is at the spec level.
Does not imply StableHLO is a runtime; it is an IR/interchange format consumed by compilers.

distractorRationales.B: Wrong claim about dynamic shape support.
distractorRationales.D: Confuses IR spec with runtime concerns.
